newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU countries blamed for EU fraud.
newsitem.headline: EU countries blamed for EU fraud.

text.p: European Union member countries will be rapped on the knuckles on Tuesday for failing to get to grips with fraud of the European Union's budget.

European Commission officials said a report by the European Court of Auditors to be unveiled at the EU Parliament on Tuesday would say that it was not the EU authorities who were responsible for the bleeding of EU money.
Areas where EU capitals could do better to fight fraud include olives, rice and feta cheese, fishing surveillance and the EU's social funds, the auditors' report for 1995 says.
Member states failed to collect several million dollars in customs and tax contributions through lax application of legislation and customs checks, it said.

The report, made available to Reuters, also criticises them for failing to track fraud of export refunds in the agricultural sector. It says the failure bled around 16 million Ecus ($19 million) from the EU budget.
EU governments failed to make registers to track refunds which went to fictional olive groves and rice fields.
"This has still not been done in the main olive producing member states four years later," the report said.

The report says that despite advances in some cases of 50 percent of the cash needed to set up sea and air surveillance to make sure fishermen are not overfishing the money was being wasted as the schemes were delayed.
It also said that EU countries were not taking adequate care of who was on the receiving end of social funds intended to help the EU's less well-off.
"Ineligible expenditures were found and unreliable technical and financial information was supplied by groups," it said.
